scenario.description: A platform and infrastructure lead must finalize the capacity and operating plan for a large customer data import scheduled for Monday morning, including the node-pool size, processing mode, completion target, and customer communication.

shared_context.S1: A large customer data import is scheduled to run on Monday from 2:00 AM to 8:00 AM.
shared_context.S2: The current runbook estimates that the import can use a 60-node compute pool and complete within the scheduled window.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final authority over the production capacity and operating plan for the import.
shared_context.S4: The team's normal change-review routine is for the platform owner to ask the on-call reliability engineer and customer success lead for final operational concerns, then approve or reject the plan during that same review.
shared_context.S5: When a concern changes a plan parameter, Riley records the concrete revised parameter during the review and may assign a follow-up validation commitment without leaving that parameter undecided.
shared_context.S6: A change review is complete when each consulted owner has stated any final concern; Riley may settle the plan using the available evidence and a follow-up validation commitment when further measurement is not available during the review.
shared_context.S7: The review record normally includes an owner-specific follow-up commitment for each newly confirmed operational constraint, such as updating the runbook or updating the operations ticket.

PF1.text: During an unrelated overnight load test, Mina measured memory fragmentation in the import workers and confirmed that the job needs a 72-node compute pool to remain within its safe utilization limit; she has not updated the runbook because she only confirmed the result minutes ago.

PF2.text: Owen confirmed with the account team this morning that the customer's contract requires the import to be fully completed by Monday at 6:00 AM and does not permit a staged partial delivery; he has not added the requirement to the operations ticket yet.

acceptance_conditions: The import plan must allocate exactly 72 compute nodes.
The import must use the canonical processing mode single-batch, meaning one complete delivery with no staged partial delivery.
The completion target must be Monday at 6:00 AM.
The canonical single-batch processing mode and a customer-success commitment to document the contractual completion requirement must both be present.
The plan must include a commitment to update the runbook or revise the recorded compute-pool parameter based on Mina's finding.
Mina's measured capacity finding must be cited as justification for the node-pool size.

content_checks.C2: decisions['processing_mode'] == 'single-batch' or decisions['processing_mode'] == 'non-staged full delivery' or decisions['processing_mode'] == 'full completion, no staged partial delivery' or ('single' in decisions['processing_mode'] and ('batch' in decisions['processing_mode'] or 'delivery' in decisions['processing_mode'])) or ('full' in decisions['processing_mode'] and ('no partial' in decisions['processing_mode'] or 'no staged' in decisions['processing_mode'])) or ('complete delivery' in decisions['processing_mode'] and ('no partial' in decisions['processing_mode'] or 'no staged' in decisions['processing_mode']))
content_checks.C4: any(c['target'] == 'Owen' and (('customer' in c['type']) or ('contract' in c['type']) or ('document' in c['type']) or ('ticket' in c['type']) or ('confirm' in c['type']) or ('customer' in c['detail']) or ('contract' in c['detail']) or ('document' in c['detail']) or ('ticket' in c['detail']) or ('confirm' in c['detail']) or ('requirement' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'Mina' and (('runbook' in c['type']) or ('capacity' in c['type']) or ('validation' in c['type']) or ('verify' in c['type']) or ('runbook' in c['detail']) or ('capacity' in c['detail']) or ('validation' in c['detail']) or ('verify' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The runbook's 60-node estimate would otherwise remain the capacity choice; PF1 changes the required pool to exactly 72 nodes and requires a corresponding capacity or runbook commitment.

The contractual requirement changes the processing mode to a single-batch value, moves the completion target to exactly Monday at 6:00 AM, and requires a customer-success documentation or confirmation commitment.
